title: Environment and process
summary: Use process.env, process.argv, stdin and exit codes to build a small command-line program.

docs.title: Node.js: How to read environment variables
Node.js: Accept input from the command line

quiz.q: What type of value is process.env.PORT when the variable PORT=3000 is set?
quiz.explain: Environment variables are always strings. Use `Number(process.env.PORT)` when you need a number.

quiz.q: PORT is NOT set. What does this print?
quiz.explain: `process.env.PORT` is `undefined` when the variable is missing, so `||` falls back to `3000`. This pattern lets the same code run on your laptop and on a server that chooses its own port.

quiz.q: By convention, which exit code tells the operating system that the program failed?
quiz.explain: `0` means success and any non-zero number, usually `1`, means failure. Tools such as npm and CI servers read this code.

quiz.q: Why keep passwords and API keys in environment variables instead of in the code?
options: The code can be shared or committed to Git without exposing the secret, and each machine can use its own value
Strings in code cannot contain symbols
quiz.explain: Secrets written in code end up in Git history and in every copy of the project. Reading them from `process.env` keeps them outside the code.

quiz.q: Complete the code that sets a failing exit code and prints the problem on the error stream.
quiz.explain: `console.error` writes to stderr, which is meant for problems. Setting `process.exitCode = 1` lets the program finish cleanly and then exit with a failure code. `process.exit(1)` ends it immediately.

exercise.task:
In `sum.js`, write a command-line program that reads numbers from standard input, **one per line**, and prints their total.

- If the input is `10`, `20` and `5` on three lines, print `Total: 35`.
- Skip empty lines.
- If there are no numbers at all, print `No numbers given` with `console.error` (not `console.log`), print nothing on standard output, and set the exit code to `1`.
- On success the exit code stays `0`.
hints: Collect the input with `process.stdin.on('data', ...)` and handle the finished text in `process.stdin.on('end', ...)`.

In the `end` handler split the text into lines, drop the empty ones with `filter`, and turn them into numbers with `Number`. If the list is empty, call `console.error` and set `process.exitCode = 1`. Otherwise add them up and print `Total: ` followed by the sum.
